questions.title: How does FeatLLM extract rules from the LLM using the two-step reasoning instruction?
questions.question_body: In Section 3.1 the paper describes a two‑step reasoning instruction: (1) infer causal relationships between features and the task without looking at the few‑shot examples, and (2) use those relationships together with the examples to deduce rules for each class. I'm unclear how this is actually enforced in the prompt. Does the LLM see the examples twice, or is there a separate prompt for each step? How do we make sure the model does not leak information from step 2 into step 1, and how is the fixed number of 10 rules per class implemented?

questions.title: Why are the learned linear weights projected onto a non‑negative subspace in Eq. (2)?
questions.question_body: The inference equation computes `logit_k^i = max(w_k, 0) · z_k^i`. The authors say this ensures that LLM‑generated features do not reduce class likelihood during learning. Could someone explain more formally why a negative weight would be problematic in this setting, and what would happen if we allowed unrestricted weights?

questions.title: What parsing strategy is used to convert natural‑language rules into executable Python code?
questions.question_body: Section 3.2 mentions that instead of writing a complex parser they ask the LLM itself to generate code based on a prompt containing the function name, input/output descriptions, and inferred rules. How robust is this approach to variations like "greater than" vs ">"? Are there any fallback mechanisms if the generated code fails to `exec()`? Also, does the parsing stage require any human‑in‑the‑loop validation?

questions.title: How does feature bagging interact with the prompt size limitation?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that bagging mitigates excessive prompt size when the number of columns is large. Is the bagging performed on columns (i.e., randomly selecting a subset of features for each ensemble trial) or on samples, or both? How is the size of each bag chosen relative to the LLM context window, and does this affect rule quality?

questions.title: What is the effect of temperature on rule diversity and ensemble performance?
questions.question_body: During ensembling, the authors increase temperature to introduce randomness in rule generation. Has any quantitative analysis been done on how temperature values (e.g., 0.3 vs 0.8) affect the diversity of extracted rules and downstream AUC? Is there a risk that higher temperature leads to more syntactic noise that harms parsing?

questions.title: Why does omitting the reasoning step cause larger performance drops in low‑shot regimes?
questions.question_body: The ablation study shows that removing the Step‑1 reasoning instruction hurts performance especially when k is small. Can we get an intuition or example of what kind of spurious rules are generated without this step, and why prior knowledge alone isn’t sufficient in such few‑shot settings?

questions.title: How are spurious correlations quantified in the Heart dataset experiment?
questions.question_body: In Section 4.2, unrelated columns from Adult are appended to Heart and performance degradation is measured. What metric was used to quantify degradation (e.g., change in AUC)? Also, how were “rules based on noisy columns” identified—by inspecting rule text or by checking which binary features fire on those columns?

questions.title: Can FeatLLM be adapted to regression tasks instead of classification?
questions.question_body: The current formulation assumes binary/multi‑class labels and uses a softmax over class logits. If we wanted to predict a continuous target, how would we modify rule extraction (e.g., generating inequality‑based rules) and the downstream model (e.g., linear regression with non‑negative weights)?

questions.title: What are the computational trade‑offs between FeatLLM’s 30 API calls and a single end‑to‑end LLM inference per sample?
questions.question_body: The paper states that FeatLLM requires only 30 API queries irrespective of test set size, whereas in‑context baselines query per test sample. Could someone break down the time/money cost of those 30 calls (including temperature setting) compared to, say, 10 000 test samples processed with an LLM at 0.02 $/1K tokens? How does this scale with dataset size?

questions.title: How does FeatLLM ensure that generated binary features are linearly independent enough for a simple linear model to learn?
questions.question_body: Since each rule yields a binary feature, many rules could be redundant or highly correlated. Does the bagging/ensemble process implicitly handle this redundancy, or would it be beneficial to add an explicit feature selection step before training the linear model?
